topics.openQuestion: What conditions favour the accuracy of readings, and how to determine the source?
topics.interpretation: The tests with absent sitters and blind ratings, the documentary surveys and the studies of trance answer different questions. Several tests report readings better recognized than the controls; others do not find this difference. Brazilian cases allow to examine the accuracy of details and the possible access to information. The cerebral correlates and the experience of mourning describe other aspects of the phenomenon. These results do not in themselves determine the source of the information.
profile: Observed findings

favourable meta-analysis; positive results in several American and Italian protocols, null results in other tests, including a Brazilian psychographic protocol. Positive documentary surveys to examine on a case-by-case basis.
Methodological robustness

Identify who knows the deceased, who leads the session and who scores the readings. Examine lures, information transmitted, generic elements, documentary checks, missing data and dependencies between readings.
Variability and study conditions
Preselection of mediums, sitter presence or absence, oral or written communication, natural sittings or constrained protocols: these differences must be documented before comparing findings.
Scope of the conclusions

Separate factual accuracy, subjective experience, brain activity and effects on mourning. Accurate information does not automatically separate psi acquisition by the living and post-mortem communication.
readingGuide: Accuracy of information
Do relatives identify a reading intended for them better than a control reading? Are its details verifiable and specific?
Experience and conditions
What do mediums and sitters describe? How do brain states, experiences and outcomes vary according to session conditions?
Origin of information

profile: Observed findings
Associations with certain rhythms, ERP differences and positive or null fMRI results. Frontal interventions form a separate program, with reported directional effects.
Methodological robustness

Control of artifacts, number of comparisons, choice of windows and regions, order of conditions and transparency of processing. A precise instrumental measure does not guarantee the validity of its interpretation.
Variability and study conditions
The participant's status, relational context, task, scanner environment and method of analysis may vary. Their role must be measured; to invoke it is not enough to explain a gap between studies.
Scope of the conclusions
Distinguish a correlate of an experience, target discrimination and causal intervention. A brain-filter theory requires predictions that separate it from other explanations.

rows: Systematic and critical review of ESP neuroimaging
143 reports, 129 studies; corpus more extensive than interpersonal correlations only
Often small samples, analytical flexibility and controls of repeated multiple comparisons in the methodological discussion.

Illustrating the importance of the signal time structure and the null model, beyond the counting of replications alone.

profile: Observed findings

Methodological robustness
Acquisition, independence of devices, autocorrelation and multiple comparisons must be considered together.
Variability and study conditions

Scope of the conclusions
These experiments primarily concern physiological association; they do not establish conscious telepathy or quantum entanglement.

topics.question: An out-of-body experience (OBE) is the feeling of being outside one's body. It can occur outside a near-death experience, particularly during sleep or deliberate attempts. This review distinguishes phenomenology, induction, physiological recording and verification of perceptions. Perceptions during resuscitation are addressed in the NDE review.
topics.handbook: Chapter 13, section on out-of-body experiences, and chapter 14 of David Acunzo for neuroscientific approaches. Selection completed by the work of 2025 and 2026.
readingGuide: Experience

Feeling outside the body, a displaced viewpoint, seeing one's body: describe precisely what is reported. An induced bodily illusion does not necessarily reproduce every dimension of a spontaneous OBE.
Physiological measurement
EEG, MRI or eye movements can document the state or time reported by the participant. A time marker is not a verification of the perception of a hidden target.
Verifiable information
Compare a narrative to a documented target or event, with time stamping, access control and independent rating. A correspondence does not locate the consciousness out of the body alone.
metrics: participants in the Weiler et al. (2026) target test
rows: 87 publications from 1987 to 2024; six documentary databases
Cartography of spontaneous and induced OBE, their characteristics and their relationship to sleep and lucid dream.
The 87 publications are not 87 tests of extrasensory perception. The review does not provide a common estimate of success on hidden targets.
21 participants; 10 report an OBE; 13 descriptions analysed

No correspondence significantly greater than random according to rank tests, individually or for all 13 descriptions. Two spontaneous descriptions of the environment are reported separately as accurate.
Spontaneous matches are not successes to the intended targets. Automated semantic scoring and small corpus define the scope of the null result.

studyGroups.title: Perception: historical experiences
studyGroups.intro: These studies looked for information or effects at the location where the participant said they were located, and the criteria for success and controls differed greatly.
rows: One participant; four nights; five-digit target out of sight from bed
A number correctly identified the fourth night, accompanied by an EEG recording. Tart defends the ESP interpretation while highlighting the inconclusive nature of this isolated study.

One case and one success. Possible access to the target and monitoring require assessment; even anomalous information acquisition would not distinguish out-of-body perception from other psi hypotheses.
Alex Tanous; 197 usable trials in 20 sessions; optical device and strain gauges
Activation of higher gauges in successful ranked trials than in failures (p < 0.05 after presentation of target) Differences are also reported before the target.
Conditional comparison in a single participant. Perception criteria and physical measurements must be distinguished; this result alone does not demonstrate physical movement outside the body.

studyGroups.title: Induction, MRI and physiological detection
studyGroups.intro: These approaches inform bodily representation and laboratory study of OBEs. Their findings concern experience and accompanying physiology, without a hidden-target perception test in the studies below.
rows: A patient assessed for epilepsy; right angular gyrus
Repeated induction of electrically stimulated decorporation sensations in this clinical observation.
Establishes a link between stimulation and experience in this case; does not suffice to explain all the OBEs or to determine the veracity of perceptions reported elsewhere.
Body vision from a camera and coordinated tactile stimulation
Experimental modification of where participants feel they are.
Sensory manipulation informs on the location of self; its equivalence with a complete spontaneous OBE must be examined, dimension by dimension.
A participant capable of voluntarily inducing an extracorporeal experience
Activity differences in regions involved in movement and bodily representation; reduced activity in the visual cortex.
Partial experience, described by the authors as an unusual form of kinaesthetic imagery. One case does not provide a universal OBE marker.
Three participants; two reported an OBE to the laboratory
One participant produces the agreed eye signal during each of three sessions to indicate the beginning of the experience.
Electro-oculography (EOG) records the eyes, not an EEG brain marker. It helps synchronise reports and measurements without verifying an actual departure from the body or distant perception.

studyGroups.title: Adapt methods and document context
studyGroups.intro: The methodological proposals are presented apart from the experimental results: they indicate conditions to be studied, without establishing in advance their role.
rows: The participant's status, relationship with the researcher, intent, skills and sense of experience
The authors propose to better articulate target testing and documentation of lived experiences, with verification of narratives and attention to context.
This text does not provide a new positive series. The proposed factors must be measured and tested; they do not constitute an already established explanation of the null results.

topics.openQuestion: Under what conditions do descriptions recorded during an OBE correspond to information inaccessible through ordinary channels?
topics.interpretation: The experience of leaving the body is an object of study distinct from the accuracy of accompanying perceptions. Induction and neuroimaging findings illuminate certain mechanisms of bodily representation. Reported perceptions require their own documentary and experimental examination; a brain correlate alone neither validates nor invalidates them.
profile: Observed findings

Circumstantiated narratives, positive historical observations, induction experiments and target tests with no significant results. Keep planned results and spontaneous observations in explicit categories.
Methodological robustness

Control access to targets, record the narrative before verification, specify the correspondence criteria and the blind. For physiology, synchronize the data with the reported experience and compare control states.
Variability and study conditions
Spontaneous, sleep-related, voluntary and stimulation-induced OBEs are not interchangeable conditions. Describe participants, context and experienced dimensions before comparing findings.
Scope of the conclusions
A mechanism of body localization does not necessarily explain the whole story. A verified perception alone would not establish a physical separation of consciousness or post-death survival.
topics.next: Combining accurate description of the experience, time stamping, targets actually inaccessible, planned and independent rating, and synchronized measurements. Analyse the planned targets separately and the verifiable spontaneous details; also document attempts without OBE.

topics.title: Verifiable perceptions during NDEs
topics.subtitle: Compare accounts with targets, witnesses and the medical timeline
topics.direction: Corroborated accounts and target tests must be distinguished
topics.summary: Verifying a resuscitation account, identifying a hidden target and studying an experience answer different questions. Prospective studies also document the medical circumstances of data collection.
topics.question: The review covers information reported during near-death experiences (NDE), especially around cardiac arrest. A resuscitation memory is not necessarily an NDE; an NDE does not necessarily include a verifiable external perception.
rows: 2,060 cardiac arrest; 140 first-phase interviews, 101 second-phase interviews
A narrative of the perception of resuscitation could be corroborated.
A substantiation of the context is not a hidden visual target identification. The moment of remembrance and the corresponding brain state remain distinct questions.
Prospective study with targets and physiological measurements
No visual targets identified; an identification of the reported auditory stimulus. EEG activities compatible with cognitive functions are observed during certain resuscitations.
The 28 interviews are not enough to define the number of evaluable visual tests. The auditory stimulus uses an ordinary sensory path. No general inference of absence of brain activity.
Construction and first validation of scale vNDE
8 criteria; 17 narratives selected to test the rating
A tool for documenting chronology, conditions of collection and third-party verification.
The agreement between evaluators does not check the events again. Here, the criteria serve as documentary benchmarks, without taking over the overall score.
topics.openQuestion: What information has been recorded, verified and located in time?
topics.interpretation: A corroborated account warrants analysis of the conditions in which it arose. On its own, it does not establish perception without sensory mediation, consciousness independent of the brain or survival after death.
profile: Observed findings
Substantiated narratives, physiological data, and target results are presented separately.
Methodological robustness
The value of a case depends on the first dated story, independent audits, actual exposure to targets, and medical chronology.
Variability and study conditions
Clinical state, resuscitation, memory timing, interviews and time to collection vary. These conditions determine what the protocol can test.
Scope of the conclusions
Documenting an experience and corroborating information are two distinct inputs; none of these steps designates its mechanism alone.
readingGuide: Observation
Record the words of the witness before verification; distinguish hidden target, corroborated medical event and subjective experience.
Explanations considered
Establish what information was accessible before, during and after resuscitation, exchanges with healthcare staff and uncertainty about timing.
Interpretation
Distinguish the accuracy of the narrative, conditions of perception and assumptions about consciousness or survival.
topics.next: Collect accounts promptly, verify facts under blinded conditions and publish successive denominators: patients exposed to targets, survivors, interviews, relevant memories and assessable trials. Retain both matches and errors.

Surveys report biographical correspondence; other work describes the experience and future of children.
Methodological robustness
The first record, witness independence, search for candidates, access to information and retention of unconfirmed statements are decisive.
Variability and study conditions
Cultural context, family relationships, age and time frame vary, and their influence requires explicit analysis, without assuming that it explains each case.
Scope of the conclusions
A correspondence is a documentary result. Interpretation in terms of transferred memory, psi or reincarnation requires additional arguments.

Interpretation

topics.title: Global Consciousness Project (GCP)
topics.subtitle: Historical GCP and GCP 2.0: results, psi selection and collective interpretation
topics.direction: Historical findings and new data must be distinguished
topics.summary: Bancel proposes psi-mediated selection of analysis windows to explain the historical result; Nelson defends a collective interpretation. GCP 2.0 introduces new equipment and publishes exploratory findings.
topics.question: Two programmes are distinguished: the formal historical experience of 1998–2015, followed by reanalyses, and the GCP 2.0, already active during its scientific presentation in 2023. The closing of the 500 events in 2015 does not mark the end of GCP research. Micro-PK trials with explicit intent remain treated in their own review.
rows: Cumulative Z ≈ 7. According to Bancel, XOR processing and synchronisation rule out a simple field acting on raw bits; the tests favour a goal-oriented psi effect.
XOR: logical operation inverting certain bits to limit biases. The conclusion concerns the models tested; it does not refute any possible conception of a collective consciousness.
Contests the obligation to act on raw bits. In particular invokes temporal and spatial structures to defend a field model.
These observations should be distinguished from the tests initially announced, and their compatibility with one model is not sufficient to exclude others.
Periods of events and related data
Report negative deviations around freely chosen windows, absent for fixed days of 24 hours; sees there a signature of psi selection.
Psi selection here refers to supposed choices guided by anomalous information. It does not imply prior consultation of the results or physical modification of the generators.
500 formal events; analysis of continuous flow
Recalls Z = 7.31 and argues for structures supporting a field model, including temporal profiles obtained by averaging across events.
The 491 events of Bancel belong to the corpus of 500: do not add up the two assessments. The analogy with EEG responses is not a measure of collective brain activity.
topics.openQuestion: What protocols would distinguish collective influence, psi selection and ordinary bias?
topics.interpretation: In Bancel's account, the experimenter effect is a psi hypothesis. People involved in the study could select favourable events and time boundaries through anomalous information, without necessarily changing the generators. This mechanism differs from ordinary statistical bias. GCP 2.0 provides different data; neither the historical score nor Bancel's conclusions automatically apply to it.
profile: Observed findings

A cumulative gap is reported in the historical corpus. In particular, GCP 2.0 reports a correlation between local and global networks during meditations; the two statistics relate to different protocols.
Methodological robustness
Examine the registry before data are accessed, selection criteria, windows and secondary analyses. A Z score is not a probability of existence of the psi.
Variability and study conditions
Compare types of events, schedules, devices, selection rules and people defining tests. The stability of a cumulative score does not identify its cause.
Scope of the conclusions

Comparing the predictions of collective influence, a psi selection by committed people and ordinary biases. A correlation between network indicators does not directly measure a collective consciousness.
readingGuide: Observation
Distinguish the statistical result, the conditions for selecting the data and the explanation of the observed deviation.
Psi selection in Bancel's account
The choice of events and windows would be guided by psi information towards favorable fluctuations. Physical action on generators is not necessary in this model.
Ordinary selection bias
Choosing after consulting the results, trying several windows or retaining the only favorable tests can produce a bias without psi. This mechanism is distinct from the Bancel hypothesis.
topics.next: Defining events, windows and analyses in advance, then comparing human choices and external criteria with predictions specific to each model. For GCP 2.0, document also the separation of local and global networks and control periods. Preregistration reduces some ordinary biases; it does not exclude, by definition, a hypothesis of psi selection.

Insufficiently documented null results are coded Z = 0. Aggregation alone does not solve selection biases, quality of checks or the independence of series.
profile: Observed findings
Historical series and their aggregation differ from the expected distribution, and the results of studies and their synthesis are not independent confirmations.
Methodological robustness
Pre-production of targets and sealed copies allow specific controls. Time stamping, file integrity, assignment of instructions, and access history remain essential.
Variability and study conditions

The delay before observation, the repetition of presentations and the role of observers vary between protocols, and these differences prevent all experiments from being treated as strictly equivalent.
Scope of the conclusions

An association between intention and sequences does not demonstrate alteration of a previously observed datum. On its own, it does not distinguish retrocausality, psi selection and ordinary explanations.

profile: Observed findings
The corpus includes excess correct responses and results close to chance. The 2024 video test reported an overall accuracy of 49.9%.
Methodological robustness
The relevant controls relate to sensory indices, sequence drawing, feedback, repeated responses from a participant, and the advertised success criterion.
Variability and study conditions
Direct staring, presence behind a window and live video are different situations. A response bias can increase success on staring trials while decreasing it on non-staring trials.
Scope of the conclusions
The conscious responses and the electrodermal reactions are two distinct measures. An observed effect in one cannot be attributed automatically to the other.

Methodological robustness

Variability and study conditions
Diagnosis, spontaneous fluctuations, treatments, fatigue, close relatives present and near death may vary. These variables should be documented, without reducing any episode to a single explanation.
Scope of the conclusions
A renewed communication is not, in itself, an acquisition of psi information. A verified perception requires a proper analysis; the implications for survival remain an additional interpretation.

profile: Observed findings

Full recordings, independent transcription, novel comprehension and production tests, detailed language-exposure history and control of the interlocutor's cues.
Variability and study conditions
Transe, hypnosis, dissociative states, childhood and neurological disorders describe different contexts. The degree of competence and its stability must be measured in each.
Scope of the conclusions
A memory whose source is forgotten can be experienced as new. Conversely, finding a skill is not enough to attribute its origin to an earlier life, to an entity or to the psi.

topics.title: Spontaneous after-death communications (ADCs)
topics.subtitle: Post-death presences, dreams and perceptions: experience, effects and verification.
topics.direction: Documented experiences; interpretations must be distinguished
topics.summary: Surveys and reviews describe experienced contact with a deceased person without a medium's involvement. Their reality as experiences and their effects on bereavement are distinct from the origin of any information received.
topics.question: What forms do these spontaneous experiences take, what consequences do they have and which elements can be independently verified? Contacts induced in therapy are covered in the clinical review.
metrics: studies in the qualitative synthesis of 2026
rows: The narratives combine the maintenance of the link, the search for meaning, comfort and sometimes conflict. The social and cultural context intervenes in their integration.
Synthesis of experience and its consequences; no causal therapeutic effects or transfer of psi information are tested.
1 004 respondents; questionnaire of 194 items; three languages
Sleeping experiences, sensory perceptions and a sense of presence; respondents often describe a comforting and meaningful experience.
Targeted recruitment of people who experienced an ADC. It neither measures population frequency nor verifies external communication.
topics.openQuestion: Do narratives containing specific information, recorded prior to confirmation, differ from other CDAs in their context or content?
topics.interpretation: The term ADC refers here to a perceived contact, without deciding on its mechanism. A reported beneficial effect deserves to be studied without itself constituting a validation of survival. The results on mourning are not a substitute for an investigation of the witness's possibly unknown information.
profile: Observed findings
Surveys describe experiences that are sometimes enduring and generally important to those reporting them. Comfort and distress must be documented separately.
Methodological robustness
Distinguish population surveys, targeted recruitment, case interviews and verification. Reanalysing the same questionnaire does not provide independent confirmation.
Variability and study conditions
Relationship with the deceased, time since death, sleep or wakefulness, culture, beliefs and reactions of others may affect descriptions and consequences.
Scope of the conclusions
This work mainly informs phenomenology and mourning. Establishing inaccessible content through ordinary channels requires an additional documentary protocol.
readingGuide: Observation
Collect the story without reducing the experience from the outset to a symptom or proof of survival.
Verification
For new information, date the first story, previous knowledge and independent confirmation.
Interpretation
Separate mechanism from experience, personal sense and effect on mourning.

topics.openQuestion: Do visitors unaware of a location's history report the same specific details before any exchange between witnesses, and do these matches persist at comparable control locations?
topics.interpretation: The convergence of narratives justifies an investigation; its significance depends on their independence, accuracy and chronology. Tests of infrasound or magnetic fields examine particular hypotheses. Their results, positive or null, do not alone solve the question of the origin of apparitions.
profile: Observed findings
Investigations find spatial clustering of experiences. Explanations using physical variables yield mixed findings depending on measures and protocols.
Methodological robustness
Compare well-known haunted places and control places, hide their history, collect narratives separately and distinguish between field correlation and experimental manipulation.
Variability and study conditions
Lighting, acoustics, expectations, familiarity with local stories, exposure duration and visitor characteristics may interact.
Scope of the conclusions
Describing an experience, identifying an environmental factor and establishing an apparition independent of the witness are three different goals.
readingGuide: Observation

Verification
Search for pre-exchange documents, records, and comparison with reference sites.
Interpretation
Test specific mechanisms without turning a local explanation or lack of explanation into a universal conclusion.

topics.openQuestion: Can one document a physical event with continuous and independent monitoring of the room, objects and participants, keeping all the sessions and data?
topics.interpretation: A significant experience in the session does not certify its physical mechanism. Conversely, a documented rigging case is not sufficient to classify all historical records. Each case must be examined according to the actual controls performed, the traces retained and the competing explanations tested.
profile: Observed findings
Archives describe apports and materialisations; current surveys also describe effects on participants. These two types of finding are not interchangeable.
Methodological robustness
Issues include continuity of observation, access to the room, object control, traceability of samples and expertise in illusionism.
Variability and study conditions
Obscurity, participant disposition, group familiarity, medium interventions and registration restrictions can change both the experience and the possibility of verification.
Scope of the conclusions
A preserved object or image requires a chain of provenance. Even an established physical anomaly would not automatically designate the identity or nature of its agent.
readingGuide: Observation
Distinguish direct perception, collective narrative and instrumental recording.
Verification
Examine the controls actually maintained during the phenomenon, the possible manipulations and the source of the traces.
Interpretation
Separate existence of an anomaly, physical mechanism and attribution to a deceased.
topics.next: Digitise historical protocols and the objections raised against them. For new studies, agree in advance on continuous monitoring, independent expertise and publication of negative observations.

topics.question: This review covers empirical study of synchronicities: questionnaires, daily follow-ups and investigations in therapeutic settings. It distinguishes experiencing a coincidence, its personal value and the possibility of a causal or acausal connection between events.
topics.openQuestion: Can a prospective journal with timed events and independent listing distinguish frequency from correspondence, attention to coincidences and assigned personal value?
topics.interpretation: The psychological significance of a coincidence can be studied without presuming its mechanism. The communication reports 24.4% success against 20% expected, p = 0.009.
Conference abstract; not a new replication or a direct IC-versus-Ganzfeld test. Limited experimenter diversity reported by the author.
topics.interpretation: Imagery induction and target performance must be evaluated separately. The 2023 findings differ by criterion, whereas the 2026 synthesis reports a cumulative deviation. Considering them together calls for examination of protocols, dependencies and study conditions.
profile: Observed findings
Positive differences are reported in the programme and its consolidation of 2026. Study 2023 does not exceed chance on direct success; another criterion reached p = 0.05.
Methodological robustness

The registered plan makes the assumptions searchable. The presence of previous beta-tests, the plurality of criteria and the inclusion of a work submitted in the synthesis must be explicitly followed.
Variability and study conditions
Duration, components of induction, beliefs, subjective states and experimenters differ. A change of experience does not guarantee a better target identification.
Scope of the conclusions
The file tests a set of inductions and precise tasks. Indirect comparisons with Ganzfeld do not allow to conclude their equivalence or superiority.

readingGuide: Lived experience
Describe the experience, its context and temporality, without deducing its mechanism from its intensity.
Comparison
Resemblance to an NDE or a psi experience is a phenomenological comparison.
Information
Accuracy requires an independent target, a planned rating and controls of available information.
rows: 139 respondents recruited from networks interested in parapsychology or psychedelic.
Associations between some experiences and some substances are described; no significant correlation between psi experience and the use of a particular substance is found.
Selection of respondents and retrospective memories; no controlled task of acquiring information.
Neurochemical models, narratives, investigations and experimental research.
The review organises work on ESP, OBEs and NDEs and discusses their methods.
Bibliographic record and abstract consulted: no calculation of cumulative effect taken here, nor quantitative conclusion from the historical corpus.
NDE-type scores increase under DMT; all participants reach the conventional threshold of the questionnaire under this condition.
Small size and subjective measurement. The protocol deals with the similarity of experiences, without a verifiable perception test or demonstration of the identity of mechanisms.

Linking subjective descriptions with psychological or neurochemical models.
Synthesis article; does not constitute a new controlled test or a psi performance meta-analysis.

The results on the intensity or similarity of the experiences do not, in themselves, establish an extrasensory gain of information. Methodological robustness

Variability and study conditions

Scope of the conclusions
A closeness of description between two states informs their phenomenology; it shows neither the same cause nor an exact external perception.

topics.title: Prospective tests of survival
topics.subtitle: Sealed messages, secret codes and combination padlocks.
topics.direction: Explicit protocols; post-mortem success not established in the selected documents
topics.summary: These tests define expected information or actions before death. Their criteria and constraints differ from spontaneous accounts or mediumship readings: secrecy, preservation, control of attempts and delayed verification.
topics.question: Can information prepared prior to death then be transmitted under conditions excluding ordinary channels, and what interpretation would allow a positive result?
readingGuide: Preparation
Define secrecy, retention, informed people and criteria for success before attempts are made.
Verification
Accounting for all possible answers and access; a solution found by cryptanalysis is not a mediumistic communication.
Interpretation
Even accurate information would require comparing information leak, chance, psi of the living and survival hypothesis.
rows: Stevenson, 1968; Stevenson, Oram & Markwick, 1989, reviewed by Willin & Matlock, 2026
Combination padlocks: proposal and historical follow-up
Secrets prepared by researchers, including Thouless and Pratt.
The SPR synthesis reports attempts without a correctly transmitted combination after death. Thouless's padlock was later opened by another method.
The originals of 1968 and 1989 have not been read in full here; the result attributed to the SPR synthesis, with its bibliography. No overall rate is calculated.
Passage II, remained unresolved after the other two passages.
The text is deciphered by computer research in books and statistical analysis of sequence of letters.
Success of an ordinary method: an old code deemed secret is not enough to guarantee the origin of a correct future response.
An archival study of the Tanagras Protocol
Six physical actions announced in envelopes deposited in 1936; archives opened in 2007.
No documentary confirmation of the expected actions is identified; several conservation, scheduling and verification difficulties are discussed.
Testing physical actions rather than reading a message. The late examination does not allow continuous control of all the places concerned.
topics.interpretation: The value of these protocols lies in the possibility of setting a target before the event. The archives consulted do not establish a post-mortem success according to the project. This informs the tests performed and their constraints; a lack of response does not separate all the assumptions regarding survival.
profile: Observed findings
The selected historical assessments report failure of communication or lack of verification. Codes have been resolved by documented cryptographic methods.
Methodological robustness
Target precision is an asset. Possible information leakage, the number of attempts, system security and preservation of documents over several decades also need examination.
Variability and study conditions
The protocols request memory of a code, verbal communication or physical action. Time, intermediaries and success criteria change; their results do not combine into a homogeneous rate.
Scope of the conclusions
A failure concerns a given procedure. A well controlled success would first establish an informational or physical correspondence; attribution to a deceased would require an additional argument.
topics.next: Establish a sustainable register of targets and attempts, independent security control and a published decision-making rule; distinguish the observed result from assumptions about its source.
topics.openQuestion: What mechanism would make a success both verifiable and discriminating between communication attributed to the deceased and other channels of access to information?

topics.title: Parapsychology and theories of perception
topics.subtitle: Historical contributions, research on experience and models to be tested
topics.direction: Documented historical and experimental contributions; theoretical extensions to test
topics.summary: Psychical research contributed to the study of nonconscious processes and unusual perceptual experiences. Work on Ganzfeld, confidence and ambiguous perceptions provides specific findings. Psi models also propose extensions to theories of perception, whose validation must be examined separately.
topics.question: How have psychical and parapsychological research helped explain how an impression becomes a perception, a judgement and a conviction? This review distinguishes documented historical contributions, findings on perception, borrowing from existing models and new hypotheses. It includes related neuroscience work while specifying its origin. Ganzfeld and RV performance are assessed in dedicated reviews.
readingGuide: Historical influence
A text, citation or collaboration must show that one research programme actually informed another. Similarity between ideas alone does not establish historical influence.
Lived experience
An impression can be fragmentary, bodily or highly convincing. Describing its form informs experience; establishing accuracy requires an independent comparison with the target.
Acquisition and construction
The transformation of information into representation is distinct from its acquisition. A model of imagery or categorization alone does not provide the channel of access to a hidden target.
Contribution and validation
A theory may clarify a question and propose tests before being confirmed. Conceptual usefulness, empirical findings and reception in other disciplines are three separate assessments.
rows: The subliminal, sensory and motor automatisms, symbolisation.
James explicitly acknowledges Myers' contribution to a psychology studying mental activity outside ordinary consciousness.
Directly documented intellectual influence. The tribute establishes neither Myers' entire model nor an exclusive historical origin for the psychology of the unconscious.
12 female participants; Ganzfeld, sleep onset and relaxed wakefulness; 241 reports associated with EEG recordings.
Ganzfeld produces greater absorption, with EEG activity close to wakefulness and without a decline in vigilance comparable to sleep onset.
Contributes to distinguishing spontaneous imagery from hypnagogia. Small sample; multiple reports from each person do not represent additional participants.
Induced imagery can occur in an activated state; alpha changes inform attention and percept formation.
Findings concern perception without structured sensory input. They do not measure distant information transfer; the synthesis reuses earlier work.
95 participants; visual and auditory noise, degraded stimuli and ESP trials; groups based on beliefs.
Comparable detection of degraded stimuli in believers and non-believers; higher confidence and more identification errors in believers. ESP findings at chance level.
Direct contribution: distinguishing perceptual sensitivity, interpretation and certainty. These groups do not represent everyone reporting exceptional experiences.
59 people in four groups crossing voice-hearing and psychotic diagnosis; conditioning, fMRI and computational modelling.
Voice-hearers are more sensitive to induced illusory sounds, with or without a diagnosis; the model distinguishes the weight of expectations from belief updating.
Including people without a disorder helps separate perceptual experience from the need for care. Neither a psi test nor evidence that predictive coding derives from parapsychology.
Sensed presences in patients and induction through sensorimotor conflict in volunteers.
A mismatch between movement and touch can produce the feeling that another person is nearby: a contribution to studying boundaries between self and other.
A causal mechanism for the induced condition. It does not by itself explain every report of presence; related research, with no parapsychological lineage established here.

studyGroups.title: Remote viewing, fragmentary impressions and awareness of accuracy
studyGroups.intro: The RV produced a vocabulary of observation and questions about the construction of the report. Their interest can be studied by comparing, with blinding, impressions, interpretations and accuracy.
rows: Drawing transmission; dissociation of shapes, transformations and associations.
Describes impressions being broken down and reorganised, drawing attention to the steps between an impression and the final drawing.
The examples illustrate a processing hypothesis. They demonstrate neither a universal law nor the identity of RV and subliminal perception.
Historical reception within the RV community
Swann's foreword and Targ's introduction to Mind to Mind.
Explicit documentary link between Warcollier's work and figures in modern RV.
This reception is insufficient to attribute all CRV stages or a transformation of general psychology to Warcollier.
Analytic overlay (AOL): interpretation added to impressions; separation of descriptions from identifications.
The method asks practitioners to identify premature categorisations. Its potential contribution is a procedure for observing the transition from impression to judgement.
The 'signal line' remains postulated. A training protocol demonstrates neither the signal's existence nor the specific efficacy of setting AOL aside.
Implicit processes, memory, subliminal perception and orientation of activity.
Psi is proposed as a continuous, nonconscious contribution to constructing experience rather than an occasional faculty.
A hypothesis generating predictions about implicit responses. Analogies with nonconscious cognition do not establish that all perception begins with psi.
122 responses from practitioners recruited through networks; memories of their sessions.
89% report knowing a feeling of accuracy; reported indicators include surprise, repetition, suddenness, vividness and emotion.
No real-time trial measuring confidence–accuracy calibration. The published study does not support attributing a Merleau-Pontian theory of RV to its authors.

studyGroups.title: Neurocognitive models: synesthesia, associations and predictions
studyGroups.intro: These models explain different possible stages of treatment. Reconciliation with a known mechanism is a hypothesis; it is necessary to check what it predicts and what has actually been measured.
rows: Two domains: origin and transfer of information; transduction, cortical processing, then cognition.
Proposes a hyper-associative mechanism akin to synaesthesia; predicts links between synaesthetic profiles and precognitive performance.
The transducer is unknown and the proposed coupling is not experimentally identified in this article. Multimodality in an account does not demonstrate cortical synaesthesia.
Synaesthesia, exceptional experience and conscious access to usually less accessible content.
Proposes that cross-modal associations make abstract or preconscious content perceptible, and also considers nonlocal sources.
The abstract presents a proposal. Ordinary implicit content and acquisition of inaccessible information require separate tests.
Free association, primary and secondary processes, free energy and symbolisation.
Connects the organisation of experience, associative transformations and generative models; proposes 'symbolising transmodality'.
The text illuminates the transformation of representations. It does not measure cerebral conversion of a psi signal or an RV-specific mechanism.
Top-down predictions and bottom-up errors in a hierarchical network exposed to images.
A precise framework for examining how expectations and data combine. Comparing it with AOL is a comparison proposed here, not a demonstrated historical lineage.
A prediction error is a calculated discrepancy, not a hidden information channel. Its existence in RV and the effect of changing its weight remain to be established.

studyGroups.title: Philosophy: selection, transmission and scope of arguments
studyGroups.intro: These approaches are not a single theory; they ask different questions: the role of the body in perceptual selection, the brain-consciousness relationship and the causal conditions of access to an object.
rows: Perception, memory and the body's possible actions.
Perception selects what matters for action; its content is not understood as an exhaustive copy of the world.
Predates modern RV. This selective function alone does not demonstrate that relaxation makes distant information accessible.
Brain–consciousness dependence and experiences studied in psychical research.
James distinguishes empirical dependence from its interpretation: production or transmission of consciousness.
Psychical research explicitly informs his argument. The logical possibility of a transmission model does not constitute experimental confirmation.
Irreducible Mind; development of Myers' and James's work.
The authors defend a transmission or filtering model to account for various psychological phenomena.

The book's thesis is verified through its institutional description. Discriminating predictions are needed to distinguish filter models from alternatives; the experience of RV alone does not settle the issue.
Beyond Physicalism; proposals about relations between mind, brain and reality.
Observations examined in psychical research serve as proposed constraints on the construction of models of mind.
Diverse models; a psi finding does not automatically imply monism, dualism or any particular theory.
Philosophical argument based on psi data
Thesis on causal closure of the physical domain; RV, ARV, presentiment and DMILS.
Examines what accepting psi findings would imply for a universal formulation of physicalism.
The argument depends on the data and its causal premises. The consulted abstract is insufficient to attribute a detailed theory of intentionality or reference to it.

profile: Observed findings
Documented influence on James; findings on Ganzfeld imagery and perceptual confidence; descriptions of RV experiences. Related neuroscience research is identified as such.
Methodological robustness
A controlled experiment, retrospective account, training manual and philosophical argument do not support the same kind of conclusion. Overlaps and extent of consultation are specified.
Variability and study conditions

Attention, absorption, expectations, sensory modalities, training and memory of target feedback may change an account. Their roles require measurement without assuming in advance that they favour or inhibit psi.
Scope of the conclusions

The best documented contribution is to study objects, non-conscious processes, and the distinction between impression, judgement and accuracy. A parapsychological origin of predictive coding or a validation of the brain filter is not established by the sources selected.
topics.interpretation: Parapsychology has chiefly contributed by making certain experiences accessible to investigation, studying their transformation into representations and proposing hypotheses about continuity between implicit processes and perception. It has also produced research on ordinary perception, particularly at the IGPP. For contemporary models, the exchange often runs from psychology and neuroscience towards the interpretation of psi. A model's added value is then measured by the observable differences it predicts beyond a new description of the same finding.
topics.openQuestion: Which indicators experienced before learning the target actually predict accuracy, and which model explains these links better than its competitors?
topics.next: Use the same scoring rules to compare perception of degraded stimuli, imagery without a target and RV with hidden targets. Collect impressions and confidence before any feedback; predefine the phenomenological indicators to test, control information leakage, then evaluate accuracy and calibration in new sessions. Separately test the effect of instructions limiting premature identifications. This protocol is a research proposal, not the outcome of a completed study.
